cards.text: Ezekiel, a priest living among the exiles by the Kebar River (Ezekiel 1:1-3), tells this one himself. Some of the elders of Israel come over and sit down in front of him. Then the word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel.

cards.question: The LORD tells Ezekiel that these elders of Israel have set up idols. Where did they set them up?

cards.text: Not on a shelf. Not in a corner. In their HEARTS. And they've set wicked stumbling blocks right in front of their own faces. That's like parking the cookie cart in the doorway and then tripping over it every single morning.

cards.question: The LORD tells Ezekiel He's ready to consult with these idol-hearted elders right away.

cards.text: So the Lord GOD gives Ezekiel a message to tell them. When any Israelite sets up idols in his heart and then comes to the prophet, the LORD will answer him.

cards.question: When an Israelite with idols in his heart comes to the prophet, the LORD will answer him according to his great ___.
The LORD says He answers an idol-hearted Israelite that way so He may take hold of the hearts of the people of Israel.

cards.text: Then God names what those idols have really done between Him and His people.

cards.question: Because of their idols, how many of the people of Israel does the LORD say are estranged from Him?

cards.text: So what's the fix? Ezekiel is told to take a message from the Lord GOD to the whole house of Israel.

cards.question: The Lord GOD tells the house of Israel: ___ and turn away from your idols.

cards.text: And turn their faces away from every one of their abominations. Not a peek. Not one last look. AWAY. That's me walking past the chocolate chips, staring at the ceiling like we've never met.
The Lord GOD's message to the house of Israel keeps going. And now He widens the circle on who this warning covers.

cards.question: Besides Israelites, who else does the LORD name in His warning about idols in the heart?

cards.text: Anyone who separates himself from God, sets up idols in his heart, and then comes to the prophet to inquire of God. That's like ghosting a friend for a whole year and then texting, "Hey, quick question."

cards.question: When someone like that comes to the prophet to inquire, the LORD says He will answer him Himself.

cards.text: The LORD Himself. And I bet it's not the answer this man was hoping for. God says He will set His face against him.

cards.question: The LORD says He will make that man a ___ and a ___.
The LORD says He will cut that idol-hearted man off from among His people.

cards.text: Then God says, "Then you will know that I am the LORD." Now He turns to the prophet in this picture. What if that prophet is enticed to speak a message?

cards.question: If the prophet is enticed to speak a message, who does the LORD say enticed him?
What does the LORD say He will do to the prophet who is enticed to speak?

answers.text: Stretch out His hand against him
Give him a brand new message
Send him back to the elders

cards.text: Destroy him from among His people Israel, God says. And they will bear their punishment, the one who came asking and the prophet both.

cards.question: How does the punishment of the one who came asking compare with the prophet's punishment?

cards.text: So why all of this? The Lord GOD says it Himself, right at the end.

cards.question: The LORD says He does all this so the house of Israel will keep its distance from Him.
So Israel will no longer stray from Him, the Lord GOD says. Then they will be My ___ and I will be their ___.

findings.problem: Stop 2's choice cards open with the same question-type sequence as Stop 1: multiple choice, true or false, fill in the blank, true or false, multiple choice (Stop 1 cards 2, 4, 6, 7, 9 and Stop 2 cards 2, 4, 6, 7, 9).

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The question says the LORD answers 'that way,' which points back to card 6. Card 6 is no longer on screen, so the question doesn't say how the LORD answers.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question uses 'someone like that,' which points back to card 3. Card 3 is no longer on screen. The question should say it means someone who separates himself from God, sets up idols in his heart and then comes to the prophet.

findings.problem: The two blanks in 'a ___ and a ___' read just as well in either order. A baker who picks 'proverb' then 'sign' could fairly argue they got it right, but the card only accepts 'sign' in blank 1 and 'proverb' in blank 2.
findings.question: When two blanks can take the right answers in either order, should both orders count as right, or should the card be reworded so only one order fits?

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Stretch out His hand against him,' is a Bible idiom. The wrong answers, 'Give him a brand new message' and 'Send him back to the elders,' sound modern and casual. That makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card opens with 'The LORD Himself,' which comes from Ezekiel 14:7 ('I the LORD will answer him Myself'). The card cites only Ezekiel 14:8, so the citation should be Ezekiel 14:7-8.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: Stop 2 has only one real joke in 15 cards (the ghosting line on card 3). Cards 1, 8, 11 and 13 read as plain narration. None of them has Papa Dorin's reactions, disbelief or self-deprecation, even where the moment could hold a laugh without muddying a fact, such as the inquirer and the prophet bearing the same punishment.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
